item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
126
ABPZ20 KNHC 292305
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Polo, located just inland in Sonora, Mexico, on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, on
Tropical Storm Rachel, located a few hundred miles southwest of
Lazaro Cardenas, Mexico, and on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E,
located over the western East Pacific.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this weekend or early next
week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development
while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Pierce/Cangialosi

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.


DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the remnants of Polo were located near
latitude 30.5 North, longitude 108.0 West. The remnants are moving
toward the northeast near 23 mph (37 km/h).
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
WIND: A Wind Advisory remains in effect for portions of southern 
New Mexico and far western Texas where strong gusty winds are 
possible tonight in association with Polo’s remnants. Refer to 
products issued by your local National Weather Service Forecast 
Office for additional information.
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane
Center on Polo.
 
$$

item.title: Remnants of Polo Forecast Discussion Number 38
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026 
458 
WTPZ42 KNHC 300232
TCDEP2
 
Remnants Of Polo Discussion Number  38
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Satellite images and surface observations indicate that Polo has
dissipated over the rugged terrain of northwestern Mexico, and this
is the last NHC advisory. However, the remnants of Polo are still
producing areas of heavy rain and gusty winds over portions of
northwestern Mexico and the southwestern U.S. The initial intensity
is estimated to be around 30 kt.
 
The remnant trough is forecast to continue to weaken, but the
associated moisture will likely produce heavy rainfall and flooding
across the Southwest U.S. and the Southern High Plains tonight and 
Wednesday morning.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 11a
item.description:
Issued at 600 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026 
519 
WTPZ33 KNHC 292342
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Intermediate Advisory Number 11A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
600 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
...RACHEL FORECAST TO BECOME A MAJOR HURRICANE LATER THIS WEEK...
...GUSTY WINDS SPREADING ALONG THE COAST OF SOUTHWESTERN MEXICO... 
 
SUMMARY OF 600 PM CST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.6N 106.3W
ABOUT 285 MI...460 KM WSW OF LAZARO CARDENAS MEXICO
ABOUT 265 MI...425 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico north of Playa Perula to Cabo
Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case over the
next 12-24 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case in the next 12-24
hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 600 PM CST (0000 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located near latitude 16.6 North, longitude 106.3 West. Rachel is 
moving toward the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h). A northwestward 
motion at a slower forward speed is expected during the next several 
days. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel is forecast to 
move parallel to, but stay offshore of, the coast of southwestern 
Mexico.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Steady to rapid strengthening is forecast during the next few 
days. Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane tonight and a major 
hurricane by Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center. Manzanillo International Airport recently reported 
sustained winds of 35 mph (56 km/h).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are spreading into the warning area 
and will continue tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in 
the watch area by tonight or Wednesday.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches, with isolated maximum totals of 12 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, Michoacán, Colima and
Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the southwestern coast 
of Mexico during the next couple of days and spread northward along 
the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula 
through the end of the week. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026 
808 
WTPZ43 KNHC 292048
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
There has been a wealth of data to parse through this afternoon with 
Rachel. On satellite imagery, Rachel is exhibiting a large 
convective burst with cloud tops below -85 C, though this burst is 
still centered a little south of the center fixes provided by the 
NOAA P-3 aircraft that conducted a research mission into the storm. 
The peak 700-mb flight level winds from the mission were 66 kt. In 
addition, there was a dropsonde launched in the radius of maximum 
wind on its east side that had 500 m average of 75 kt, which using  
a typical reduction factor yields 60 kt. Furthermore, there was a 
uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) that was launched in the same area in 
the boundary layer, finding 975-mb winds also up to 75 kt. An 
experimental reduction factor developed by CIRA indicated this value 
translates to a 10-meter sustained wind of 63 kt. All of the above 
data suggests that Rachel is nearly a hurricane, and the initial 
intensity is set at 60 kt this advisory. A 1620 UTC ASCAT-B pass, in 
addition to the aircraft data, were both useful to adjust the 34- 
and 50-kt radii this afternoon. 

Rachel continues to move off to the northwest, with aircraft fixes 
indicating a motion of 305 degrees at 12 kt. A mid-level ridge 
located over central Mexico is expected to steer the tropical 
cyclone in that same direction over the next 12-24 h. However, an 
upper-level cutoff low moving across the four corners region of the 
southwestern United States will soon erode this ridge, leading to a 
significant slowdown in Rachel's motion. After 48 h, another 
mid-level ridge begins to build in over California and Nevada behind 
this cutoff low as it ejects into the central Plains. The net effect 
of this synoptic pattern is Rachel should then turn more westward, 
but still at a slow forward motion. Some of the reliable track aids 
have made a southward shift in Rachel's track this afternoon, and 
the latest NHC track forecast has been shifted in that direction, 
blending the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA), the Google 
DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI), and their new experimental model 
(WN3I). 

Shear analysis from UW-CIMSS indicates that the northeasterly shear 
that had been affecting Rachel is starting to decrease, and both the 
EC- and GFS-based SHIPS guidance show this lowering below 15 kt in 
24 h. In addition, the latest forecast track brings Rachel initially 
to the north of the cool wake left behind by Polo, with nearby ocean 
drifters still showing sea-surface temperatures (SSTs) in the 29-30 
C range still. Thus as the shear decreases, and assuming Rachel's 
core is becoming more vertically aligned, the short-term intensity 
has been raised and now shows a period of rapid intensification from 
24-48 h, making it a 105 kt major hurricane at the end of that time 
frame. After that time, as Rachel turns westward, it will finally 
pass over Polo's cool wake, where another drifter in that vicinity 
showing SSTs much lower, in the 26-27 C range, and that combined 
with Rachel's slow motion will likely lead to weakening in 60-96 h. 
The latest NHC intensity forecast remains on the upper-end of the 
guidance, closest to HCCA through 48 h, but then falls back closer 
to the guidance mean in 72-120 h.  
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of
Mexico, tropical-storm-force winds are expected along a portion of
the coast of southwestern Mexico in the Tropical Storm Warning area
today or tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in the
watch area tonight or on Wednesday.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will bring locally heavy rainfall to 
portions of coastal southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico during
the next several days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/2100Z 16.0N 105.7W   60 KT  70 MPH
 12H  30/0600Z 17.3N 107.0W   70 KT  80 MPH
 24H  30/1800Z 18.2N 108.0W   85 KT 100 MPH

$$

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E was located near latitude 13.8 North, longitude 130.2
West. The depression is moving toward the east-southeast near 9 mph
(15 km/h) and this motion is expected to continue over the next
couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next couple of
days, and this system is expected to degenerate into a post-tropical
cyclone by Thursday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).

----------------------
None

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 292034
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Tropical Depression Nineteen's convection has dwindled quite a bit 
over the last several hours. The system's low-level center remains 
completely exposed, with lingering convective activity lying several 
dozen miles to the north of the circulation. Scatterometry data from 
this afternoon just clipped the storm's eastern flank, so TD 19's 
initial intensity will hedge more towards TAFB's latest Dvorak 
estimate of 2.0/30 kt, remaining steady from the last advisory.

Satellite imagery suggests that forward speed has slowed as well, 
with the initial motion set at 85/6 kt. The depression is generally 
expected to remain on an eastward trajectory as it is steered by a 
northward-displaced equatorial trough. Little was changed in the 
track forecast from the previous advisory, as models are largely in 
good agreement on the storm's path. Only slight adjustments in 
forward speed were made to better follow current trends. 

Several environmental factors will inhibit further development of 
the depression. Moderate vertical wind shear, drying mid-level air, 
and marginal SSTs left in the wake of the remnants of Odalys are 
likely to keep the system from reaching tropical storm strength. 
Diurnal convection cycles may allow the system to briefly flirt with 
tropical storm strength, however simulated satellite imagery across 
global models depict little to no convection for this system over 
the next 48 h. The latest intensity forecast moves up the 
depression's post-tropical transition time to Thursday afternoon, 
and dissipation is forecast shortly thereafter.
